spec_match.rationale: Targets both ImageData ends of the feature: new ImageData(w, h, { colorSpace }) construction with the colorSpace property readback, and getImageData(..., { colorSpace }) conversion, exactly as the HTML pixel-manipulation section defines them.

interactive.rationale: A colour input plus draw-and-read-back button pushes a real pixel through all four spaces and prints the returned bytes; a second button constructs ImageData in every space and reads the tag back.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises picking a colour and comparing the raw bytes per space, which is what both tables deliver.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported linear rows print the browser's verbatim TypeError, the explanation distinguishes the still-working srgb/display-p3 conversions from the rejected linear ones, and the byte comparison explains why 8-bit linear stores band.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5122501071994880, the spec's pixel-manipulation section, MDN ImageData.colorSpace, and siblings.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite assertions imagedata-srgb-linear-constructs, imagedata-display-p3-linear-constructs, and getimagedata-converts-into-srgb-linear (with a numeric linear-vs-gamma byte bound) mirror this page's exact contract; suite verified executing on the /conformance/ route.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable here): ?autorun=1 DOM grep shows srgb bytes [224,64,16], display-p3 bytes [207,77,40] (a real conversion) and verbatim TypeErrors on both linear rows; screenshots at 1280 and 360 read; zero page console errors over CDP.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the supported or explicit unsupported-fallback branch on load plus imagedata-round-trip-ran and imagedata-ctor-matrix-ran with row payloads; all speculative calls are wrapped in try/catch.

design_system.rationale: Styles.css variables throughout, dark buttons set both background and color, focus-visible outlines, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Native color input with a visible label, buttons with text labels and 44px targets, captioned tables with scoped headers, role=status support banner, aria-live explanation output, swatch has an aria-label that updates with the chosen colour.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No page-level horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (CDP-measured); wide tables scroll in their own containers; both class screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Show a putImageData composition of linear-tagged pixels once a 155 browser is available
openQuestions.detail: The construction table proves tagging, but on a browser that accepts the linear spaces the page could additionally putImageData a linear-tagged block onto an srgb canvas and read the composed result back, demonstrating the composition direction of the conversion. Blocked on a runtime that accepts the enum values; the current page states the honest TypeError instead.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible data table results announce updates
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use real tables with caption/scope for tabular results and text equivalents (aria-live) for state that changes after interaction.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both result matrices are semantic tables with captions and scoped column headers; the interpretation paragraph is an aria-live output updated on every run.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never let wide tabular data force page overflow; give it a scrollable container with a min-width table.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Both tables live in overflow-x:auto wrappers (min-width 560px table); CDP confirmed scrollWidth == innerWidth at 360px.

summary: Covers the ImageData half of the v155 feature: construction tagging and getImageData conversion, with real per-space byte readouts and verbatim TypeErrors where the browser rejects the linear values. Verified in headless Chromium 141 at both device classes with clean console.
